title: Coupled-Mode Equations with Arbitrary Mode Combinations for Kinetic-Inductance Superconducting Traveling-Wave Parametric Devices: Theory and Experimental Validation
authors: F. Patricio Mena, Camilo Espinoza, Ryan O. Berriel, Ricardo Finger, David J. Thoen
abstract: The coupled-mode equations (CMEs) have proven very successful in describing parametric processes in nonlinear optics. More recently, the same formulation has been used to model microwave superconducting parametric amplifiers and frequency multipliers. However, when applied to the microwave regime, not all assumptions remain valid and losses play a more dramatic role. Here, we revisit the CMEs applied to traveling-wave superconducting amplifiers to include losses and provide a formulation that enables their systematic derivation for any combination of traveling waves. As examples, we discuss the impact of unwanted harmonics and intermodulation products on parametric amplification, as well as harmonic generation. We verify that, if not properly accounted for, device performance can deviate considerably from the ideal case. Furthermore, using a superconducting CPW-based artificial transmission line and combining an independent experimental determination of its nonlinear parameter $I'_*$ with simulations of its linear properties, we obtain a parameter-free validation of this formulation. The nonlinear parameter was determined to be $I'_* \approx 27$ mA which, surprisingly, scales with the theoretical depairing current and not with the much smaller critical current of the device. For the validation, we measured multiple-harmonic generation and found excellent agreement between theory and experiment. The fact that $I'_* \gg I_C$ has direct implications for device design.
summary: This work presents an advanced theoretical framework using Coupled-Mode Equations (CMEs) to model parametric processes in superconducting transmission lines, systematically accounting for losses. The theory is rigorously validated by comparing simulations against microwave measurements of harmonic generation. The key finding confirms that the device's nonlinearity scales with its intrinsic depairing current, providing a robust tool for designing high-performance quantum/classical superconducting devices.
main_problem: To develop a general theoretical framework using Coupled-Mode Equations (CMEs) that accurately models parametric processes in superconducting traveling-wave devices, specifically incorporating losses and arbitrary combinations of interacting waves.
main_result: The authors successfully derived a generalized CME formulation validated by experimental measurements showing excellent agreement for harmonic generation. Crucially, the nonlinear parameter scales with the intrinsic depairing current rather than the measured critical current.
method: The methodology combines theoretical derivation using projection methods on telegrapher's equations to yield CMEs, followed by rigorous validation through microwave measurements of $S_{21}$ variation and harmonic generation.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting CPW-based artificial transmission line exhibiting quadratic nonlinearity in its inductance. The model uses CMEs to describe the spatial evolution of multiple interacting wave amplitudes ($A_m$) across different frequency modes.
key_observables: Signal gain, harmonic generation power ratios ($P_B/P_A$), relative phase variation of $S_{21}$ with DC current, and the nonlinear parameter $I'_*$.
important_parameters: $I'_*$ (nonlinear parameter), $I_{	ext{dep}}$ (theoretical depairing current), $\gamma_m$ (propagation constant), and characteristic impedance ($Z_{Cm}$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve treating the current as a superposition of plane waves, using the Slowly-Varying Envelope Approximation (SVEA) for simplification, and assuming the general CME structure holds despite losses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the theoretical model's applicability across various mode combinations (e.g., harmonic generation), show measured $S_{21}$ vs. DC current data fitted by the theory, and present simulated/measured power flow for multiple harmonics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need to generalize CMEs for lossy superconducting systems, deriving the general CME formulation applicable to any mode combination, detailing specific physical examples (harmonic generation, FWM), and finally validating this comprehensive model using detailed microwave measurements on a fabricated sample.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity/microwave physics, the underlying mathematical structure—the use of coupled differential equations to describe energy exchange between multiple interacting modes in a nonlinear medium—is highly analogous to models used in quantum optics and open quantum systems theory.
